venue.name: Nuyumbalees Cultural Centre
venue.description: Nuyumbalees Cultural Centre is the Kwakwaka'wakw cultural centre and museum at Cape Mudge on Quadra Island, run by the Nuyumbalees Museum Society. The society was founded in 1975 by hereditary and elected chiefs to negotiate the return of the potlatch collection and regalia confiscated under the anti potlatch laws, and the centre opened in 1979 as the first facility of its kind in Canada built on a First Nation reserve to house a repatriated collection. Most of the collection belonged to Chief Billy Assu. Alongside the indoor collection there is a native garden looking out over Discovery Passage, a touchscreen with stories from community elders, and the House of Eagles carving shed next to the garden.
venue.seasonal_notes: Both versions of their website carry a notice saying the centre is temporarily closed and transitioning to an opening date. One page gives June 3, 2025 and the other gives June 2026.

programs.name: Self-guided visit
programs.description: Admission is listed as $10.00 for an adult and $5.00 for a senior, youth, student or child. They take Visa, Mastercard, American Express, debit and cash, and do not accept personal cheques. The collection is generally self-guided and staff are on hand to answer questions. Outside there is a native garden looking over Discovery Passage with a place to sit and tell stories, a touchscreen carrying stories from community elders and the history of the fishing industry, and the House of Eagles carving shed beside the garden. These prices sit on the older version of their website and carry no date.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the collection of masks and potlatch regalia at their own pace, reading and asking staff questions, then go outside to the garden above the water where they can use the touchscreen of elders' stories and look at the carving shed.
programs.our_note: Admission is charged per person with no group rate published, so a class of twenty at $5.00 each adds up before you have booked anything. Getting there means the ferry from Campbell River across to Quadra Island, which is worth building into the timing. Call before you commit, because their pages still carry a closure notice with two different reopening dates on them.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing on the site covers washrooms, an indoor lunch space or step free access, so ask about all three when you call. The collection is indoors and there is a garden outside beside the water.
programs.evidence: The Collection is generally self-guided and visitors are welcome to take their time to read and learn the many aspect of our sacred traditions.

programs.name: Tours and education programs
programs.description: Their directions page asks anyone wanting tours, education, or language and cultural programs to call at least two weeks in advance. The site does not say what a session covers, how long it runs, what it costs or what ages it suits. Elsewhere the centre says replica ceremonial masks were made for educational use there so that children and visitors can learn about Kwakwaka'wakw culture, history and dance through hands on cultural experiences.
programs.our_note: Two weeks is the least notice they ask for, and with the closure notice sitting on their site you will want to make that call early anyway. Nothing about the session itself is published, so ask what it covers, how long it runs and what it costs. Ask as well whether they can take the age group you are bringing.
programs.practical_summary: Booking is by phone with at least two weeks notice. Price, length, group size, and anything about washrooms or a lunch space are not published, so the call has to cover all of it.
programs.evidence: For Tours/Education, Language/Cultural Programs please call at least two weeks in advance.

images.alt: A long red-brown wood building with a steep sloping roof and a round-roofed wing, a carved pole beside its covered entrance, and a path curving up to the door.
Two painted carved posts with outstretched wings hold up a carved beam in an open timber shelter, framing a view across the water to a far shore.
A black and white photograph of a display wall crowded with carved masks, carved figures and a long carved plank, with a small typed label card among them.

gaps: The centre runs two websites. nuyumbaleesmuseumsociety.com is the current one and museumatcapemudge.com is the older one, and the older one is where the admission prices and the note about tours and education programs sit.
The admission prices are on the older site and carry no year or season, so check they still hold before quoting them to parents.
The site never says whether school groups or daycare groups are welcome, and no minimum age is published.
No group rate, class size limit, session length or booking form is published.
months unknown: neither site says what months the centre or its programs run, beyond the notice about being temporarily closed.

Nothing is published about washrooms, an indoor lunch space, a wet weather plan, step free or stroller access, or where a bus can park. Getting there involves the BC Ferries crossing from Campbell River to Quadra Island, which the site links to but does not describe for groups.
No coordinates are published on either site, so the address is recorded for geocoding in a later pass.
The street address is published as 34 Weway Road, Cape Mudge. The only postal code given anywhere, V0P 1N0, belongs to their PO Box in Quathiaski Cove rather than to the building.

The site writes a file name into the alt attribute of the photograph on its home page, which is an accessibility failure a screen reader will read out loud. All three alt texts here were written by us after opening each image in a browser and looking at it, and are marked as generated.

The newer site carries two more large photographs, a studio portrait of one person and a single painted mask on a plain wall. Neither was recorded: the portrait is a person rather than the place, and the mask shot shows nothing that helps a group picture the visit.

THIS PASS (2026-09-07): opened the home page photograph in a browser and replaced its file name alt text with a description of what is in the frame, and took the larger version of that image the site also serves. Added two photographs from the older site, the carved posts in the garden shelter and the collection display wall, both with written alt text. Re-checked both websites: the older one still says the reopening date is June 3, 2025 and the newer one still says June 2026, so that disagreement stands and remains recorded in conflicts.

The mailto link on the older site's directions page points at nuyumbaleesculturecenter@gmail.com while the visible text on the same line reads nuyumbaleesculturalcentre@gmail.com. The newer site's email link is an unedited Wix placeholder pointing at info@mysite.com. Because of that the booking email is left blank and both addresses are recorded as a conflict.
The Centre page on the new site is still unedited Wix placeholder text, so it yielded nothing.
This is the cultural centre at Cape Mudge on Quadra Island. It is a different venue from Wei Wai Kum House of Treasures in Campbell River.

conflicts.note: They keep two versions of their website and both say the centre is closed and getting ready to reopen. One gives a date in June 2025 and the other June 2026. Ring them before you plan the trip, because the ferry makes this an expensive one to get wrong.
Their two websites give different email addresses. If one bounces, try the other. The phone number is the same on both, so calling is the surer route.
